title: Microsoft Copilot: Agent Mode in PowerPoint builds presentations from Work IQ
notes: claim 51: severity blocker on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents sensitivity-label inheritance for new Copilot presentations, but the briefing presents it as an unanswered question and says further detail is undocumented. The risk rationale also overstates the content Copilot can use: being able to access a file does not override encryption and extraction restrictions.

claims.claim: Full work data through Work IQ and semantic indexing is available only to users with the Microsoft Copilot licence.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a user licence using Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: PowerShell enables Restricted Content Discovery using Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true.
claims.quote:
Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: How source-file sensitivity labels carry into the generated deck is an unanswered question.
claims.quote:
the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.
If multiple files are used to create new content, the sensitivity label with the highest priority is used for label inheritance.
claims.fix: Remove the question 'How do sensitivity labels on source files carry into the generated deck?'. Microsoft documents inheritance for newly created Copilot in PowerPoint content and selection of the highest-priority label when multiple files are used at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot.

claims.claim: Anything a user can reach can end up in a generated deck.
claims.quote:
If the user has VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot doesn't summarize the content, but it can return a link so the user can open it outside Copilot.
Copilot and agents can't access content protected by DKE.
claims.fix: Replace 'anything a user can reach can end up in a deck' with 'relevant authorised source content can end up in a deck'. This removes the universal claim without adding new scope or changing the supported release-note statement.
